text:
sam_rawls: quick heads-up — did a 90m perf sweep on the prefix-heavy workload with prefix cache ON. saw weird batch formation: lots of tiny batches when cache-hit ratio > 0.6, p99 latency climbs. thinking we should try a cache-hit-aware admission heuristic (virtual length inflation).
marta: can you paste the numbers?
sam_rawls: sure — from the run: `throughput=480req/s`, `p50=52ms`, `p95=210ms`, `p99=1.3s` when hit_ratio=0.72. when hit_ratio~0.15 throughput=610req/s p99=430ms.
benji: interesting — cache hits compress prefill so kernels pick short-seq fast-path but admission end-stacks small batches? sounds like packing prefers fill_by_tokens rather than fill_by_clients.
anna_k: what if we inflate virtual_token_length for hits by a factor (e.g. +64 tokens) so they don't get preferentially packed into tiny microbatches? simple config: 
```json
{"admission": {"hit_inflation": 64, "target_tokens": 1024, "max_batch_size": 32}}
```
sam_rawls: that's exactly the idea I prototyped. with +48 inflation p99 drops to ~520ms and throughput recovers to ~580req/s. cost impact negligible.
ryan: watch kernel choice — I saw a subtle regression where kernel-selector picks the small-seq kernel for hits but that path moves more work to CPU for KV unpack; on some nodes that flips perf. we need a kernel-score that accounts for kv-unpack-cost not just seq-len.
benji: yeah — kernel selector should consider `kv_hit=true` as a separate feature. maybe bump heuristic weight for memory-copy cost.
perf-bot: perf run uploaded — s3://redwood-test/perf/2481234567/summary.json :thumbsup:
sam_rawls: proposed experiment plan: (1) enable hit_inflation=48 globally on one pool, (2) add kernel-feature kv_hit to selector (low risk flag off), (3) collect 4x 30m windows ramp. can someone own A/B metrics and rollback?
marta: i'll own metrics/dashboard and traces. I'll add a synthetic workload with mixed prompt lengths to catch regressions.
ryan: I'll prototype kv_hit feature in selector and add a small regression test for CPU-fallback.
benji: add a canary with different inflation values (0/32/48/80) so we can curve fit. also capture packing histogram (batch token counts).
sam_rawls: perfect. i'll open a short PR with config and a patch to admission code and link the run.
anna_k: if we see oscillation (hit ratio swings fast) we should add a smoothing window to inflation signal (exp moving average).
benji: agreed. also add a budget gate: never inflate if queue_token_budget < 128 to avoid starving cold traffic.
sam_rawls: noted. will include budget gate and ema smoothing. target rollout tomorrow morning. :rocket:
